item.title: Iran War Live Updates: Trump to Speak to Nation Tonight on War
item.summary: The president has offered muddled signals about the aims of the war, though he has said it will end soon. U.S. intelligence agencies believe Iran is not currently willing to negotiate.

item.title: Evacuated From War-Torn Gaza, 11 Toddlers Return Home to Hugs and Tears
item.summary: The Palestinian children were born prematurely in the early days of the war and moved from a besieged hospital to Egypt. They have now returned home to the enclave, which lies in ruins.

item.title: Israel’s Message to a Broad Swath of Lebanon: Shiites Must Go
item.summary: Israel has issued sweeping evacuation warnings, and pressed some Christian and Druse leaders to expel Shiite Muslims from southern towns, the leaders said.

item.title: The Sailors Stranded in the Persian Gulf
item.summary: Thousands of civilian sailors have been stranded for more than a month in waters surrounded by a conflict zone because of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: French Prosecutors Link Foiled Attack on American Bank to a Pro-Iranian Group
item.summary: The group is suspected of involvement in a string of attacks on Jewish targets in Belgium, Britain and the Netherlands.

item.title: 29 Killed in Russian Military Plane Crash in Crimea
item.summary: Investigators cited a possible technical malfunction.

item.title: Europe Has a ‘Guns vs. Butter’ Problem. War in Iran Makes It Worse.
item.summary: After decades of prioritizing domestic over military spending, the continent’s leaders are trying to pivot. That is straining national budgets and could anger voters.

item.title: Iran Is Skeptical About Diplomacy, U.S. Intelligence Says
item.summary: Any decision by Iran to keep fighting would complicate President Trump’s stated goal of trying to end the war within weeks.

item.title: Trump’s Endgame in Iran?
item.summary: We look at what has changed, and what hasn’t, as a result of the joint U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

item.title: Iran’s President Suggests Diplomatic Engagement Possible in Letter to U.S. Public
item.summary: The letter, by President Masoud Pezeshkian of Iran, was at times defiant, patronizing or conciliatory, and came hours before President Trump was set to address the American people on the war.
